sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhīmasena yamau cobhau pāñcāli ca nibodhata nāsti bhūtasya nāśo vai paśyatāsmān vanecarān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Bhīmasena, both twins, and Pāñcālī — hear me. There is truly no destruction of any living being; look upon us as wanderers in the forest.

sanskrit: durbalāḥ kleśitāḥ smeti yad bravīthetaretaram aśakye 'pi vrajāmeti dhanaṃjayadidṛkṣayā
english: Though you say to one another, 'We are weak and suffering,' yet we travel even toward what seems impossible, out of longing to see Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: tan me dahati gātrāṇi tūlarāśim ivānalaḥ yac ca vīraṃ na paśyāmi dhanaṃjayam upāntike
english: This burns my limbs like fire burns a heap of cotton — the fact that I do not see the hero Dhanañjaya near at hand.

sanskrit: tasya darśanatṛṣṇaṃ māṃ sānujaṃ vanam āsthitam yājñasenyāḥ parāmarśaḥ sa ca vīra dahaty uta
english: The thirst to see him burns me, dwelling in the forest with my younger brothers; and the injury done to Yājñasena's daughter also burns me, O hero.

sanskrit: nakulāt pūrvajaṃ pārthaṃ na paśyāmy amitaujasam ajeyam ugradhanvānaṃ tena tapye vṛkodara
english: I do not see that Pārtha, elder brother of Nakula, of immeasurable might, that unconquerable wielder of the fierce bow — by that I am tormented, O Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: tīrthāni caiva ramyāṇi vanāni ca sarāṃsi ca carāmi saha yuṣmābhis tasya darśanakāṅkṣayā
english: I roam the pleasant tīrthas, forests, and lakes together with you, yearning for the sight of him.

sanskrit: pañca varṣāṇy ahaṃ vīraṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ dhanaṃjayam yan na paśyāmi bībhatsuṃ tena tapye vṛkodara
english: For five years I have not seen the hero Dhanañjaya, true to his word, the Bībhatsu — by that I am tormented, O Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: taṃ vai śyāmaṃ guḍākeśaṃ siṃhavikrāntagāminam na paśyāmi mahābāhuṃ tena tapye vṛkodara
english: That dark-complexioned Guḍākeśa, who walks with the gait of a lion in his stride — the great-armed one I do not see; by that I am tormented, O Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: kṛtāstraṃ nipuṇaṃ yuddhe pratimānaṃ dhanuṣmatām na paśyāmi naraśreṣṭhaṃ tena tapye vṛkodara
english: That master of weapons, skilled in battle, the equal of all bowmen — the foremost among men I do not see; by that I am tormented, O Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: carantam arisaṃgheṣu kālaṃ kruddham ivāntakam prabhinnam iva mātaṅgaṃ siṃhaskandhaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Dhanañjaya, who moves among enemy hosts like Death when enraged, like a maddened elephant, lion-shouldered —

sanskrit: yaḥ sa śakrād anavaro vīryeṇa draviṇena ca yamayoḥ pūrvajaḥ pārthaḥ śvetāśvo 'mitavikramaḥ
english: — who is not inferior to Śakra in valor or in wealth, that Pārtha elder brother of the twins, the white-horsed one of immeasurable prowess —

sanskrit: duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭaḥ svakṛtenānivartinā ajeyam ugradhanvānaṃ taṃ na paśyāmi phalgunam
english: — seized by great sorrow that does not depart through any deed of mine, I do not see that unconquerable, fierce-bowed Phalguna.

sanskrit: satataṃ yaḥ kṣamāśīlaḥ kṣipyamāṇo 'py aṇīyasā ṛjumārgaprapannasya śarmadātābhayasya ca
english: He who is ever disposed to forbearance even when insulted by the most trivial; to one who has entered the path of righteousness he is a giver of peace and of fearlessness —

sanskrit: sa tu jihmapravṛttasya māyayābhijighāṃsataḥ api vajradharasyāpi bhavet kālaviṣopamaḥ
english: — but to one who acts crookedly and seeks to kill by deceit, he would be like deadly poison even to the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: śatror api prapannasya so 'nṛśaṃsaḥ pratāpavān dātābhayasya bībhatsur amitātmā mahābalaḥ
english: Even to an enemy who has come to him for refuge, that Bībhatsu is not cruel; he is glorious, a giver of safety, boundless in spirit and great in might.

sanskrit: sarveṣām āśrayo 'smākaṃ raṇe 'rīṇāṃ pramarditā āhartā sarvaratnānāṃ sarveṣāṃ naḥ sukhāvahaḥ
english: He is the refuge of us all, the crusher of enemies in battle, the gatherer of every jewel, the bringer of happiness to all of us.

sanskrit: ratnāni yasya vīryeṇa divyāny āsan purā mama bahūni bahujātāni yāni prāptaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: It was by his valor that I once possessed many divine jewels of many kinds, which Suyodhana has now obtained.

sanskrit: yasya bāhubalād vīra sabhā cāsīt purā mama sarvaratnamayī khyātā triṣu lokeṣu pāṇḍava
english: It was by the strength of his arms, O hero, that the hall of mine once stood, renowned throughout the three worlds, filled with every kind of gem, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: vāsudevasamaṃ vīrye kārtavīryasamaṃ yudhi ajeyam ajitaṃ yuddhe taṃ na paśyāmi phalgunam
english: Equal to Vāsudeva in valor, equal to Kārtavīrya in battle — unconquerable, never defeated in war — that Phalguna I do not see.

sanskrit: saṃkarṣaṇaṃ mahāvīryaṃ tvāṃ ca bhīmāparājitam anujātaḥ sa vīryeṇa vāsudevaṃ ca śatruhā
english: Born after Saṃkarṣaṇa of great valor and you, O Bhīma the unconquered, he is born equal in valor to Vāsudeva and is the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: yasya bāhubale tulyaḥ prabhāve ca puraṃdaraḥ jave vāyur mukhe somaḥ krodhe mṛtyuḥ sanātanaḥ
english: In the strength of his arms and in power he is the equal of Purandara; in swiftness he equals the wind; in countenance the Moon; in wrath Death eternal.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ taṃ naravyāghraṃ sarve vīra didṛkṣavaḥ pravekṣyāmo mahābāho parvataṃ gandhamādanam
english: All of us, eager to see that tiger among men, O hero, shall enter mount Gandhamādana, O great-armed one.

sanskrit: viśālā badarī yatra naranārāyaṇāśramaḥ taṃ sadādhyuṣitaṃ yakṣair drakṣyāmo girim uttamam
english: Where vast Badarī and the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa stand — that most excellent mountain, ever inhabited by yakṣas, we shall behold.

sanskrit: kuberanalinīṃ ramyāṃ rākṣasair abhirakṣitām padbhir eva gamiṣyāmas tapyamānā mahat tapaḥ
english: On foot we shall go to that lovely lake of Kubera, guarded by rākṣasas, performing great austerities as we travel.

sanskrit: nātaptatapasā śakyo deśo gantuṃ vṛkodara na nṛśaṃsena lubdhena nāpraśāntena bhārata
english: That region cannot be reached by one who has not performed austerities, O Vṛkodara; nor by one who is cruel, or greedy, or not at peace, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatra sarve gamiṣyāmo bhīmārjunapadaiṣiṇaḥ sāyudhā baddhanistriṃśāḥ saha viprair mahāvrataiḥ
english: There we shall all go, seeking the footsteps of Bhīma and Arjuna, armed and with swords strapped on, together with the brāhmaṇas of great vows.

sanskrit: makṣikān maśakān daṃśān vyāghrān siṃhān sarīsṛpān prāpnoty aniyataḥ pārtha niyatas tān na paśyati
english: One who is undisciplined encounters flies, mosquitoes, gadflies, tigers, lions, and reptiles; one who is disciplined does not see them, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ niyatātmānaḥ parvataṃ gandhamādanam pravekṣyāmo mitāhārā dhanaṃjayadidṛkṣavaḥ
english: We, with disciplined souls, eating sparingly, eager to see Dhanañjaya, shall enter mount Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te śūrās tatadhanvānas tūṇavantaḥ samārgaṇāḥ baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇāḥ khadgavanto 'mitaujasaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those heroes, with their bows strung and quivers full, arrows set, wrist-guards fastened, bearing swords, of immeasurable might —

sanskrit: parigṛhya dvijaśreṣṭhāñ śreṣṭhāḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām pāñcālīsahitā rājan prayayur gandhamādanam
english: — the foremost among all bowmen, taking with them the best among the twice-born, accompanied by Pāñcālī, O king, set out for Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: sarāṃsi saritaś caiva parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca vṛkṣāṃś ca bahulacchāyān dadṛśur girimūrdhani nityapuṣpaphalān deśān devarṣigaṇasevitān
english: They beheld lakes and rivers and mountains and forests, trees with abundant shade, and on the mountain-summits regions ever bearing flowers and fruit, frequented by hosts of divine seers.

sanskrit: ātmany ātmānam ādhāya vīrā mūlaphalāśanāḥ cerur uccāvacākārān deśān viṣamasaṃkaṭān paśyanto mṛgajātāni bahūni vividhāni ca
english: Placing themselves in themselves, subsisting on roots and fruits, those heroes roamed regions of varied terrain, difficult and perilous, beholding many diverse species of wild animals.

sanskrit: ṛṣisiddhāmarayutaṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ priyam viviśus te mahātmānaḥ kiṃnarācaritaṃ girim
english: Those great-souled ones entered the mountain frequented by ṛṣis, siddhas, and immortals, beloved of gandharvas and apsarases, and haunted by kiṃnaras.

sanskrit: praviśatsv atha vīreṣu parvataṃ gandhamādanam caṇḍavātaṃ mahad varṣaṃ prādurāsīd viśāṃ pate
english: As the heroes were entering mount Gandhamādana, a fierce wind arose and a great rain fell, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: tato reṇuḥ samudbhūtaḥ sapatrabahulo mahān pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca dyāṃ caiva tamasāvṛṇot
english: Then a great cloud of dust arose, laden with leaves, and covered the earth, the sky, and the heavens with darkness.

sanskrit: na sma prajñāyate kiṃ cid āvṛte vyomni reṇunā na cāpi śekus te kartum anyonyasyābhibhāṣaṇam
english: With the sky veiled by dust, nothing could be discerned; nor were they able to call out to one another.

sanskrit: na cāpaśyanta te 'nyonyaṃ tamasā hatacakṣuṣaḥ ākṛṣyamāṇā vātena sāśmacūrṇena bhārata
english: They could not see one another, their eyes overcome by the darkness, dragged about by the wind laden with powdered stone, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: drumāṇāṃ vātabhagnānāṃ patatāṃ bhūtale bhṛśam anyeṣāṃ ca mahījānāṃ śabdaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: A great sound arose from trees broken by the wind and crashing heavily to the ground, and from other things of the earth.

sanskrit: dyauḥ svit patati kiṃ bhūmau dīryante parvatā nu kim iti te menire sarve pavanena vimohitāḥ
english: "Is the sky falling to the earth? Are the mountains splitting apart?" — thus all of them thought, bewildered by the storm.

sanskrit: te yathānantarān vṛkṣān valmīkān viṣamāṇi ca pāṇibhiḥ parimārganto bhītā vāyor nililyire
english: Feeling their way by hand along nearby trees, anthills, and uneven ground, fearful of the wind, they crouched and took shelter.

sanskrit: tataḥ kārmukam udyamya bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ kṛṣṇām ādāya saṃgatyā tasthāv āśritya pādapam
english: Then Bhīmasena of great might, lifting his bow, took hold of Kṛṣṇā and, meeting her, stood leaning against a tree.

sanskrit: dharmarājaś ca dhaumyaś ca nililyāte mahāvane agnihotrāṇy upādāya sahadevas tu parvate
english: The Dharmarāja and Dhaumya took shelter in the great forest, while Sahadeva took shelter on the mountain, carrying the sacred fire-vessels.

sanskrit: nakulo brāhmaṇāś cānye lomaśaś ca mahātapāḥ vṛkṣān āsādya saṃtrastās tatra tatra nililyire
english: Nakula, the other brāhmaṇas, and the great ascetic Lomaśa, trembling with fear, found trees here and there and crouched beneath them.

sanskrit: mandībhūte ca pavane tasmin rajasi śāmyati mahadbhiḥ pṛṣatais tūrṇaṃ varṣam abhyājagāma ha
english: When the wind had weakened and the dust had settled, a heavy rain quickly came with great drops.

sanskrit: tato 'śmasahitā dhārāḥ saṃvṛṇvantyaḥ samantataḥ prapetur aniśaṃ tatra śīghravātasamīritāḥ
english: Then streams mixed with hailstones, covering everything on all sides, fell incessantly there, driven by the swift wind.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāgaragā āpaḥ kīryamāṇāḥ samantataḥ prādurāsan sakalusāḥ phenavatyo viśāṃ pate
english: Then the waters rushing toward the ocean, scattered on all sides, appeared turbid and foaming, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: vahantyo vāri bahulaṃ phenoḍupapariplutam parisasrur mahāśabdāḥ prakarṣantyo mahīruhān
english: Carrying abundant water, covered with foam-rafts, roaring with great noise, they flowed in all directions, dragging away great trees.

sanskrit: tasminn uparate varṣe vāte ca samatāṃ gate gate hy ambhasi nimnāni prādurbhūte divākare
english: When the rain ceased and the wind became calm, when the waters had flowed into the low places and the sun appeared —

sanskrit: nirjagmus te śanaiḥ sarve samājagmuś ca bhārata pratasthuś ca punar vīrāḥ parvataṃ gandhamādanam
english: — they all came out slowly and assembled together, O Bhārata; and the heroes set out again toward mount Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prayātamātreṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu padbhyām anucitā gantuṃ draupadī samupāviśat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, no sooner had the great-souled Pāṇḍavas set out on foot than Draupadī, unaccustomed to traveling thus, sat down.

sanskrit: śrāntā duḥkhaparītā ca vātavarṣeṇa tena ca saukumāryāc ca pāñcālī saṃmumoha yaśasvinī
english: Exhausted, overcome by grief, and by that wind and rain, and by reason of her delicacy, the glorious Pāñcālī fainted.

sanskrit: sā pātyamānā mohena bāhubhyām asitekṣaṇā vṛttābhyām anurūpābhyām ūrū samavalambata
english: Overwhelmed by her swoon, the dark-eyed one clutched both her rounded, shapely thighs with her arms.

sanskrit: ālambamānā sahitāv ūrū gajakaropamau papāta sahasā bhūmau vepantī kadalī yathā
english: Clinging to both her thighs, which resembled elephant trunks, she suddenly fell to the ground, trembling like a plantain tree.

sanskrit: tāṃ patantīṃ varārohāṃ sajjamānāṃ latām iva nakulaḥ samabhidrutya parijagrāha vīryavān
english: As she fell, the shapely one clinging like a vine, valiant Nakula ran to her and caught her.

sanskrit: nakula uvāca rājan pāñcālarājasya suteyam asitekṣaṇā śrāntā nipatitā bhūmau tām avekṣasva bhārata
english: Nakula said: O king, this dark-eyed daughter of the Pāñcāla king has fallen exhausted to the ground — look to her, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: aduḥkhārhā paraṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpteyaṃ mṛdugāminī āśvāsaya mahārāja tām imāṃ śramakarśitām
english: She who is undeserving of suffering has met with the greatest grief; she who walks with gentle steps — reassure her, O great king, she who is worn down by fatigue.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rājā tu vacanāt tasya bhṛśaṃ duḥkhasamanvitaḥ bhīmaś ca sahadevaś ca sahasā samupādravan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At his words the king, seized with great grief, and Bhīma and Sahadeva, all quickly ran to her.

sanskrit: tām avekṣya tu kaunteyo vivarṇavadanāṃ kṛśām aṅkam ānīya dharmātmā paryadevayad āturaḥ
english: Seeing her, pale-faced and thin, the son of Kuntī, righteous in soul, took her in his lap and lamented in distress.

sanskrit: kathaṃ veśmasu gupteṣu svāstīrṇaśayanocitā śete nipatitā bhūmau sukhārhā varavarṇinī
english: How can she who was accustomed to well-spread couches in guarded palaces, who deserves comfort, the fair-complexioned one, now lie fallen on the bare ground?

sanskrit: sukumārau kathaṃ pādau mukhaṃ ca kamalaprabham matkṛte 'dya varārhāyāḥ śyāmatāṃ samupāgatam
english: How have her delicate feet and her lotus-bright face, which deserve all honor, become darkened today on my account?

sanskrit: kim idaṃ dyūtakāmena mayā kṛtam abuddhinā ādāya kṛṣṇāṃ caratā vane mṛgagaṇāyute
english: What has been done by me, foolish and fond of gambling, bringing Kṛṣṇā along to roam this forest swarming with herds of deer?

sanskrit: sukhaṃ prāpsyati pāñcālī pāṇḍavān prāpya vai patīn iti drupadarājena pitrā dattāyatekṣaṇā
english: "Pāñcālī will find happiness upon obtaining the Pāṇḍavas as husbands" — so thinking, her father king Drupada gave away this long-eyed one.

sanskrit: tat sarvam anavāpyaiva śramaśokād dhi karśitā śete nipatitā bhūmau pāpasya mama karmabhiḥ
english: Without obtaining any of that, worn by toil and grief, she lies fallen on the ground because of my sinful deeds.

sanskrit: tathā lālapyamāne tu dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire dhaumyaprabhṛtayaḥ sarve tatrājagmur dvijottamāḥ
english: As the Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira lamented thus, Dhaumya and all the other foremost twice-born came there.

sanskrit: te samāśvāsayām āsur āśīrbhiś cāpy apūjayan rakṣoghnāṃś ca tathā mantrāñ jepuś cakruś ca te kriyāḥ
english: They comforted him and honored him with blessings; they also muttered protective spells against evil spirits and performed the rites.

sanskrit: paṭhyamāneṣu mantreṣu śāntyarthaṃ paramarṣibhiḥ spṛśyamānā karaiḥ śītaiḥ pāṇḍavaiś ca muhur muhuḥ
english: As the great seers recited mantras for her well-being and the Pāṇḍavas again and again touched her with cool hands —

sanskrit: sevyamānā ca śītena jalamiśreṇa vāyunā pāñcālī sukham āsādya lebhe cetaḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
english: — and as she was attended by a cool breeze mixed with water, Pāñcālī found comfort and slowly, gradually, regained her senses.

sanskrit: parigṛhya ca tāṃ dīnāṃ kṛṣṇām ajinasaṃstare tadā viśrāmayām āsur labdhasaṃjñāṃ tapasvinīm
english: Taking hold of that wretched Kṛṣṇā, they then let the suffering one, now restored to consciousness, rest on a deerskin spread on the ground.

sanskrit: tasyā yamau raktatalau pādau pūjitalakṣaṇau karābhyāṃ kiṇajātābhyāṃ śanakaiḥ saṃvavāhatuḥ
english: The twins, with hands calloused from the bowstring, gently massaged her feet, rosy on their soles, adorned with auspicious marks.

sanskrit: paryāśvāsayad apy enāṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca ca kuruśreṣṭho bhīmasenam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: The Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira also comforted her, and the foremost of the Kurus spoke these words to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: bahavaḥ parvatā bhīma viṣamā himadurgamāḥ teṣu kṛṣṇā mahābāho kathaṃ nu vicariṣyati
english: "Many are the mountains, O Bhīma, uneven and hard to traverse with snow; how shall Kṛṣṇā wander through them, O great-armed one?"

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca tvāṃ rājan rājaputrīṃ ca yamau ca puruṣarṣabhau svayaṃ neṣyāmi rājendra mā viṣāde manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Bhīmasena said: I myself shall carry you, O king, and the princess, and the twin bulls among men, O lord of kings — do not let your mind fall into despondency.

sanskrit: atha vāsau mayā jāto vihago madbalopamaḥ vahed anagha sarvān no vacanāt te ghatotkacaḥ
english: Or else Ghaṭotkaca, that winged one born of me, equal in strength to me, shall carry all of us at your command, O sinless one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca anujñāto dharmarājñā putraṃ sasmāra rākṣasam ghaṭotkacaś ca dharmātmā smṛtamātraḥ pitus tadā kṛtāñjalir upātiṣṭhad abhivādyātha pāṇḍavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Permitted by the Dharmarāja, he called to mind his rākṣasa son; and Ghaṭotkaca, righteous in soul, the moment he was remembered by his father, appeared with folded hands and saluted the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāṃś ca mahābāhuḥ sa ca tair abhinanditaḥ uvāca bhīmasenaṃ sa pitaraṃ satyavikramaḥ
english: And the great-armed one, of true valor, was greeted by them and saluted the brāhmaṇas; then he spoke to his father Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: smṛto 'smi bhavatā śīghraṃ śuśrūṣur aham āgataḥ ājñāpaya mahābāho sarvaṃ kartāsmy asaṃśayam tac chrutvā bhīmasenas tu rākṣasaṃ pariṣasvaje
english: "I have been remembered by you and have come quickly, eager to serve; command me, O great-armed one — I will do everything, without doubt." Hearing this, Bhīmasena embraced the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dharmajño balavāñ śūraḥ sadyo rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ bhakto 'smān aurasaḥ putro bhīma gṛhṇātu mātaram
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: He is learned in dharma, strong, and brave; he is at once a bull among rākṣasas; he is devoted to us and is a natural son — let him, O Bhīma, carry his mother.

sanskrit: tava bhīma balenāham atibhīmaparākrama akṣataḥ saha pāñcālyā gaccheyaṃ gandhamādanam
english: By your strength, O Bhīma of exceedingly terrible prowess, I shall go unharmed together with Pāñcālī to Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhrātur vacanam ājñāya bhīmaseno ghaṭotkacam ādideśa naravyāghras tanayaṃ śatrukarśanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Understanding his brother's words, Bhīmasena, that tiger among men, instructed his son Ghaṭotkaca, the crusher of foes.

sanskrit: haiḍimbeya pariśrāntā tava mātāparājitā tvaṃ ca kāmagamas tāta balavān vaha tāṃ khaga
english: "O son of Hiḍimbā, your unconquered mother is utterly exhausted; and you, dear son, are able to move at will and are mighty — carry her, O winged one."
